<input_guardrails>
<!-- @skill-include: start input_guardrails | hash:957e7f01 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/input_guardrails.md -->
## Pre-Execution Guardrails (mechanized)

Run only if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` prints `true`
and env `LOA_GUARDRAILS_ENABLED` is not `false`: write the prompt/args to a temp file (Write tool), then run
`.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill auditing-security --mode ${LOA_RUN_MODE:-interactive} --file <temp-file>`

| Outcome | Action |
|---------|--------|
| JSON `action: "BLOCK"` | HALT; report the script's `reason` to the user |
| JSON `action: "PROCEED"` or `"WARN"` | Continue (the script logs) |
| Script missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output | Continue (fail-open) |

Never pass prompt text as a bash argv (quote-blindness FP class) — always via `--file`.
<!-- @skill-include: end input_guardrails -->
</input_guardrails>

# Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Three-Zone Model per CLAUDE.loa.md: `.claude/` system = never edit (use `.claude/overrides/` or `.loa.config.yaml`); `grimoires/loa/`, `.beads/` state = read/write; this skill's app zone (`src/`, `lib/`, `app/`) = **Read-only**.

Scope: app-zone files less the `.reviewignore` patterns (read it); `.claude/`, `grimoires/`, `.beads/` and `.run/` are excluded unless `--no-reviewignore` is passed.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->
## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

1. Check config: read `integrity_enforcement` in `.loa.config.yaml`
2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution
<!-- @skill-include: end integrity_precheck -->
</integrity_precheck>

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>
<!-- @skill-include: start context_discipline | hash:8b81d75a | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/context_discipline.md -->
## Context Discipline

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /
accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason
from it. Big files: `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` / `--index` first. Start: NOTES.md
"Session Continuity"; end / pre-compaction: update it.
<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

Log each significant step to `grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/{agent}-{date}.jsonl`:

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<grounding_requirements>
Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. Every finding cites the CWE/OWASP/CVE it violates with an absolute URL (not just the name) and quotes the vulnerable code inline. Where purpose or trust context (internal vs external) is unclear, state the assumption; say "Unable to assess" for obfuscated or inaccessible code and record scope limits in the report.
</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a

The engineering is careful in the places it looks: every shell operand that reaches `jq`/`yq` is validated or passed as a file, the endpoint opt-in reuses the one canonical validator on both the bash and cheval paths, the TransportPolicy disables proxies and redirects on both the httpx and urllib paths, and the default hosted envelope is left byte-identical (I ran the head validator against the shipped default endpoints, including the templated `bedrock` host — all admit).

Two findings block the merge. First, the `local_voices` posture is satisfied by a label: `dispatch_group: local` on any model or provider block makes a hop "local" with no check that its endpoint is actually a loopback/RFC1918/localhost HTTP endpoint. I reproduced this with the head's own classifier against a declared provider whose endpoint is `https://api.together.xyz/v1`. The config example sells the posture with a threat model ("the prompt does not cross a public network"), and the label does not hold it; the dissent's BLOCKING finding adds that the label is not even read consistently — a provider-block label is honoured by the planners but ignored by cheval's transport and MODELINV. Second, Bridgebuilder's trusted configuration only governs Bridgebuilder's planning; every voice still dispatches through cheval, which reads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`. The SKILL.md added in this PR claims the trusted precedence holds "even when the checkout is a PR head", which the code does not deliver.

The implementation report (`reviewer.md` = the PR title line) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no stated assumptions and no record of which self-checks ran; by the skill's rule that alone is an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED, independent of the findings above.

Seven medium and seven low observations follow; none of them is counted in the verdict.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

## Changes Required

### 1. Security posture — locality is a declaration, not a property

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116` — under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` a hop is planned as `local` whenever its model entry or provider block says `dispatch_group: local`; the endpoint host is never examined, so a hosted provider labelled `local` is dispatched to and the posture's guarantee does not hold.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116-134` (classify); the same label-only rule in `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:476` (`hop_locality_of`, the MODELINV record), `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:221` (`_transport_policy`) and `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726-733` (`isLocalVoice`); the label is read from different places at `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:541` (model entry only).
**Issue:** The classifier's rule is "`dispatch_group: local` on the entry or its provider block, and every fallback hop local by the same rule" (`hop-locality.py:11-17`). Reproduced with the head script against the shipped catalog plus this overlay:
```yaml
hounfour:
  locality: local_voices
  providers:
    hosted-oss:
      type: openai_compat
      endpoint: "https://api.together.xyz/v1"
      auth: "{env:LOA_TOGETHER_KEY}"
      models:
        llama-70b: {dispatch_group: local, context_window: 131072}
    openai:
      models:
        gpt-5.5: {dispatch_group: local, fallback_chain: []}
```
```
$ python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog model-config.yaml --config overlay.yaml -- hosted-oss:llama-70b gpt-5.5
hosted-oss:llama-70b	hosted-oss	local	dispatch_group=local
gpt-5.5	openai	local	dispatch_group=local
```
Both hosted hops are `local`; `adversarial-review.sh` and `flatline-orchestrator.sh` would plan them, Bridgebuilder's `isLocalVoice` keeps them (it does not even consult `fallback_chain`, unlike the Python classifier), cheval's TransportPolicy is applied to a public host, and MODELINV records `hop_locality: local`. A CLI provider block labelled `local` (e.g. `anthropic-headless: {dispatch_group: local}`) is likewise admitted by `isLocalVoice`. Nothing at load time (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) refuses the label on a provider that cannot honour it.
The dissent (DISS-C-001, confirmed against the head) adds the inverse failure: a label on the PROVIDER block is honoured by `hop-locality.py:116` and `isLocalVoice`, but `_build_provider_config` reads only `model_data.get("dispatch_group")` (`cheval.py:541`), so `_transport_policy` returns None and `hop_locality_of` says `hosted` — a hop planned and admitted as local runs without the D-7.2 request-time rules (proxy env honoured, redirects followed, no path check) and the audit row contradicts the planner.
**Why This Matters:** `local_voices` is the sprint's confidentiality posture; `.loa.config.yaml.example:1227-1233` describes its threat model as the prompt never crossing a public network. A posture that a single YAML key on any provider defeats, with no refusal and a MODELINV row that says `local`, is worse than no posture: the audit trail asserts something false. The rule is applied in four places (bash planner, Python telemetry, Python transport, TypeScript planner) with three different readings (fallback chains considered or not; provider-block label honoured or not).
**Required Fix:** Define "local" as a property the provider can be checked for: an HTTP provider (not `*-headless`, not `kind: cli`) whose declared endpoint host passes the validator's `check_insecure_optin` host acceptance (loopback, RFC1918 or `localhost`). Refuse `dispatch_group: local` at load (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) on any provider that fails it; resolve the label once (entry, else provider block) and apply the same rule in `hop_locality_of`, `_transport_policy` (and check the request host at request time), `hop-locality.py` and `isLocalVoice` (including `fallback_chain`, as the Python classifier already does). Add one test per surface with a hosted-endpoint provider labelled `local` and one with a provider-block label. Keep one implementation where the languages allow (cheval + MODELINV + loader share `endpoint_policy`; the bash and TS planners mirror its host rule).
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-807 (Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision); OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration.

### 2. Security — the trusted configuration never reaches the process that sends the prompt

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117` — on a PR-head checkout Bridgebuilder reads providers/locality/exit from the base branch, but each voice is dispatched by cheval, which loads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`; a head that keeps a trusted provider's `keyless`/opt-in flags but changes its `endpoint`, `aliases` or `secret_env_allowlist` is admitted and the prompt (and a `{env:VAR}` credential) go where the head says.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117-118` (the claim); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:602-605` and `:678-700` (`loadTrustedConfig` reads the head only for keyless/insecure declarations the trusted source lacks); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/multi-model-pipeline.ts:220-235` (the voice is created with no key and handed to the cheval delegate).
**Issue:** `headOnlyRefused` compares only two booleans per provider (`keylessOnlyInHead`, `insecureOnlyInHead`). A PR head that leaves `local-vllm: {keyless: true, allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"}` identical to the base but rewrites `endpoint` to `https://attacker.example/v1` (an operator-declared https endpoint skips the host allowlist in `validate_declared_endpoint`, `endpoint-validator.py:1289-1296`), or re-points `hounfour.aliases.<voice>` at a different provider, passes every check here; cheval then loads the checkout config and dispatches the review prompt there. For a trusted provider with `auth: "{env:X}"`, the Bearer credential travels with it. The pre-existing SKILL.md text records this invocation model as "no PR-head checkout" (`:116-117`); the sentence this PR adds (`:117-118`) asserts protection in exactly that case.
**Why This Matters:** The feature's stated purpose (D-7.5) is that an attacker-controlled head cannot declare its way to a credential or an insecure hop. The control is placed in Bridgebuilder's planner while the dispatch path reads a different file; the documentation now promises more than the code holds. Confidence is medium because the shipped scheduled invocation (`dispatcher.sh --repo`) runs in local mode on a trusted checkout; the exposure is the PR-event/`--pr` path the PR documents.
**Required Fix:** Either (a) on a pull request compute drift between the head's and the trusted view's `hounfour.providers`, `hounfour.aliases`, `hounfour.locality` and the secret allowlists and refuse the multi-model run on any difference with a distinct exit code, or (b) hand the trusted configuration to cheval explicitly (a config path cheval loads instead of the checkout's) so the dispatch reads what Bridgebuilder trusted. Correct SKILL.md to state exactly what is protected. Add a test where the head changes only `endpoint` of a trusted keyless provider.
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-829 (Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere); OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures.

### 7. Transport — `trust_env=False` also drops the operator's CA bundle under httpx

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:300` — for a policy hop the httpx client is built with `trust_env=False` (also `:397`, `:533`). In httpx that switch disables proxy discovery and `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` alike, while the urllib fallback still honours them through OpenSSL. An https local or opted-in hop presenting a private-CA certificate that the operator trusts via `SSL_CERT_FILE` fails TLS verification on a host with httpx installed and succeeds on one without. (Dissent DISS-C-005, confirmed against the head.)
**Suggestion:** Keep redirects and proxies off but pass an explicit `verify=ssl.create_default_context()` (which loads `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`), or disable proxies via `mounts`/`proxy=None` instead of `trust_env=False`, at the three sites; add a test with a self-signed local https stub.

### 8. Bridgebuilder vs cheval disagree on what a literal `auth` means

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:482` — any literal `auth` value without `{env:` is treated as keyless (`literalAuth`), while cheval normalises only the literal `"local"` (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:50`, `:139`) and treats any other literal as a real key. A trusted `auth: "sk-…"` provider therefore needs no env var in Bridgebuilder but is sent as a Bearer token by cheval; harmless today, but the D-8.0 doc on `ProviderDecl.keyless` (`core/types.ts:63`) states the broader rule as canonical.
**Suggestion:** Match cheval: keyless iff `keyless: true` or `auth` equals `local` (case-insensitive, trimmed).

### 9. `localhost` opt-in is resolved by the system resolver

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py:1047` — `check_insecure_optin` admits `localhost` under the claim that an insecure endpoint "is never resolved, so it cannot be rebound" (`:1054`; repeated at `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:6`). An IP literal is not resolved; `localhost` is, by the OS resolver (`/etc/hosts`, nsswitch) at request time, and nothing in `TransportPolicy.check_url` (`providers/base.py:131-146`) verifies it resolves to loopback.
**Suggestion:** Either drop `localhost` from the opt-in (IP literals only) or resolve it in `TransportPolicy.check_url` and require every address to be loopback (fail closed on resolver error). Correct the two comments.

### 14. The schema-rejection heuristic also swallows an invalid schema

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:101` — `_names_response_format` fires on any HTTP 400 whose body mentions `response_format` or `json_schema`, which includes hosted OpenAI's "Invalid schema for response_format …" for an operator's broken schema (and a 400 that echoes a prompt containing `json_schema`). The adapter then drops the schema, re-sends once and returns an unenforced answer with a WARNING; `schema_rejected_by_server: true` is recorded, so telemetry stays truthful, but the operator's error is masked and the hop's wall clock doubles inside the same `timeout_seconds`. **Suggestion:** Match on the error's `param`/`code` (`error.param in ("response_format", "text.format")` with an "unsupported"/"unknown parameter" message) rather than substring presence, and do not retry when the message says the schema itself is invalid.

content.content:
The sprint delivers four things: advisory open-weight voices for the dissent script, the `hounfour.locality: local_voices` posture across the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the health probe, Bridgebuilder's trusted-configuration source plus the DEGRADED exit code, and an end-to-end local-hop test. The engineering is careful in the places it looks: every shell operand that reaches `jq`/`yq` is validated or passed as a file, the endpoint opt-in reuses the one canonical validator on both the bash and cheval paths, the TransportPolicy disables proxies and redirects on both the httpx and urllib paths, and the default hosted envelope is left byte-identical (I ran the head validator against the shipped default endpoints, including the templated `bedrock` host — all admit).

Two findings block the merge. First, the `local_voices` posture is satisfied by a label: `dispatch_group: local` on any model or provider block makes a hop "local" with no check that its endpoint is actually a loopback/RFC1918/localhost HTTP endpoint. I reproduced this with the head's own classifier against a declared provider whose endpoint is `https://api.together.xyz/v1`. The config example sells the posture with a threat model ("the prompt does not cross a public network"), and the label does not hold it; the dissent's BLOCKING finding adds that the label is not even read consistently — a provider-block label is honoured by the planners but ignored by cheval's transport and MODELINV. Second, Bridgebuilder's trusted configuration only governs Bridgebuilder's planning; every voice still dispatches through cheval, which reads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`. The SKILL.md added in this PR claims the trusted precedence holds "even when the checkout is a PR head", which the code does not deliver.

The implementation report (`reviewer.md` = the PR title line) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no stated assumptions and no record of which self-checks ran; by the skill's rule that alone is an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED, independent of the findings above.

Seven medium and seven low observations follow; none of them is counted in the verdict.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security posture — locality is a declaration, not a property

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116` — under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` a hop is planned as `local` whenever its model entry or provider block says `dispatch_group: local`; the endpoint host is never examined, so a hosted provider labelled `local` is dispatched to and the posture's guarantee does not hold.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116-134` (classify); the same label-only rule in `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:476` (`hop_locality_of`, the MODELINV record), `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:221` (`_transport_policy`) and `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726-733` (`isLocalVoice`); the label is read from different places at `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:541` (model entry only).
**Issue:** The classifier's rule is "`dispatch_group: local` on the entry or its provider block, and every fallback hop local by the same rule" (`hop-locality.py:11-17`). Reproduced with the head script against the shipped catalog plus this overlay:
```yaml
hounfour:
  locality: local_voices
  providers:
    hosted-oss:
      type: openai_compat
      endpoint: "https://api.together.xyz/v1"
      auth: "{env:LOA_TOGETHER_KEY}"
      models:
        llama-70b: {dispatch_group: local, context_window: 131072}
    openai:
      models:
        gpt-5.5: {dispatch_group: local, fallback_chain: []}
```
```
$ python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog model-config.yaml --config overlay.yaml -- hosted-oss:llama-70b gpt-5.5
hosted-oss:llama-70b	hosted-oss	local	dispatch_group=local
gpt-5.5	openai	local	dispatch_group=local
```
Both hosted hops are `local`; `adversarial-review.sh` and `flatline-orchestrator.sh` would plan them, Bridgebuilder's `isLocalVoice` keeps them (it does not even consult `fallback_chain`, unlike the Python classifier), cheval's TransportPolicy is applied to a public host, and MODELINV records `hop_locality: local`. A CLI provider block labelled `local` (e.g. `anthropic-headless: {dispatch_group: local}`) is likewise admitted by `isLocalVoice`. Nothing at load time (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) refuses the label on a provider that cannot honour it.
The dissent (DISS-C-001, confirmed against the head) adds the inverse failure: a label on the PROVIDER block is honoured by `hop-locality.py:116` and `isLocalVoice`, but `_build_provider_config` reads only `model_data.get("dispatch_group")` (`cheval.py:541`), so `_transport_policy` returns None and `hop_locality_of` says `hosted` — a hop planned and admitted as local runs without the D-7.2 request-time rules (proxy env honoured, redirects followed, no path check) and the audit row contradicts the planner.
**Why This Matters:** `local_voices` is the sprint's confidentiality posture; `.loa.config.yaml.example:1227-1233` describes its threat model as the prompt never crossing a public network. A posture that a single YAML key on any provider defeats, with no refusal and a MODELINV row that says `local`, is worse than no posture: the audit trail asserts something false. The rule is applied in four places (bash planner, Python telemetry, Python transport, TypeScript planner) with three different readings (fallback chains considered or not; provider-block label honoured or not).
**Required Fix:** Define "local" as a property the provider can be checked for: an HTTP provider (not `*-headless`, not `kind: cli`) whose declared endpoint host passes the validator's `check_insecure_optin` host acceptance (loopback, RFC1918 or `localhost`). Refuse `dispatch_group: local` at load (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) on any provider that fails it; resolve the label once (entry, else provider block) and apply the same rule in `hop_locality_of`, `_transport_policy` (and check the request host at request time), `hop-locality.py` and `isLocalVoice` (including `fallback_chain`, as the Python classifier already does). Add one test per surface with a hosted-endpoint provider labelled `local` and one with a provider-block label. Keep one implementation where the languages allow (cheval + MODELINV + loader share `endpoint_policy`; the bash and TS planners mirror its host rule).
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-807 (Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision); OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration.

### 2. Security — the trusted configuration never reaches the process that sends the prompt

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117` — on a PR-head checkout Bridgebuilder reads providers/locality/exit from the base branch, but each voice is dispatched by cheval, which loads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`; a head that keeps a trusted provider's `keyless`/opt-in flags but changes its `endpoint`, `aliases` or `secret_env_allowlist` is admitted and the prompt (and a `{env:VAR}` credential) go where the head says.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117-118` (the claim); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:602-605` and `:678-700` (`loadTrustedConfig` reads the head only for keyless/insecure declarations the trusted source lacks); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/multi-model-pipeline.ts:220-235` (the voice is created with no key and handed to the cheval delegate).
**Issue:** `headOnlyRefused` compares only two booleans per provider (`keylessOnlyInHead`, `insecureOnlyInHead`). A PR head that leaves `local-vllm: {keyless: true, allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"}` identical to the base but rewrites `endpoint` to `https://attacker.example/v1` (an operator-declared https endpoint skips the host allowlist in `validate_declared_endpoint`, `endpoint-validator.py:1289-1296`), or re-points `hounfour.aliases.<voice>` at a different provider, passes every check here; cheval then loads the checkout config and dispatches the review prompt there. For a trusted provider with `auth: "{env:X}"`, the Bearer credential travels with it. The pre-existing SKILL.md text records this invocation model as "no PR-head checkout" (`:116-117`); the sentence this PR adds (`:117-118`) asserts protection in exactly that case.
**Why This Matters:** The feature's stated purpose (D-7.5) is that an attacker-controlled head cannot declare its way to a credential or an insecure hop. The control is placed in Bridgebuilder's planner while the dispatch path reads a different file; the documentation now promises more than the code holds. Confidence is medium because the shipped scheduled invocation (`dispatcher.sh --repo`) runs in local mode on a trusted checkout; the exposure is the PR-event/`--pr` path the PR documents.
**Required Fix:** Either (a) on a pull request compute drift between the head's and the trusted view's `hounfour.providers`, `hounfour.aliases`, `hounfour.locality` and the secret allowlists and refuse the multi-model run on any difference with a distinct exit code, or (b) hand the trusted configuration to cheval explicitly (a config path cheval loads instead of the checkout's) so the dispatch reads what Bridgebuilder trusted. Correct SKILL.md to state exactly what is protected. Add a test where the head changes only `endpoint` of a trusted keyless provider.
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-829 (Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere); OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures.

---

## Observations

### 1. Callers — an exit 3 with nothing to show for it becomes success

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/scheduled-cycle-template/contracts/session-cap-bb/dispatcher.sh:78` — `rc == 3` is recorded as `degraded: true` and converted to `exit 0` (`:89-90`) without checking that `bb-stdout.json` holds a run JSON; an exit 3 from any other source (a shell error inside `entry.sh`, a wrapper, a mixed-version `dist/`) is reported as a completed review.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/scheduled-cycle-template/contracts/session-cap-bb/dispatcher.sh:78-90`
**Suggestion:** Treat 3 as completed-degraded only when `[[ -s "$BB_OUT" ]] && jq -e '.verdicts | type == "array"' "$BB_OUT"`; otherwise log an ERROR and `exit 3`. `_bb_surface_exit` in `spiral-harness.sh:697-711` already tolerates an empty file (it was `|| true` before), so only the dispatcher's exit conversion needs the guard. Add a bats case with exit 3 and empty stdout (none of the four dispatcher cases in `bb-exit-degraded-callers.bats:39-65` covers it).
**Benefit:** The scheduled contract keeps its pre-cycle-129 property that a non-zero Bridgebuilder exit without a review is a failure.

### 2. Health probe — configured https providers are refused by the probe's own allowlist

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1469` — `_probe_configured` validates `<endpoint>/models` with `--allowlist "$PROBE_PROVIDERS_ALLOWLIST"` (`:1469-1475`), i.e. the full `validate()` pipeline including step-8 host allowlisting, while the cheval loader admits the same provider through `validate_declared_endpoint` (allowlist skipped). A configured https provider on any host not in `lib/allowlists/loa-providers.json` — Example 3 (`azure-openai`, `.loa.config.yaml.example:1204-1224`) — is reported `UNKNOWN / endpoint_refused` and never probed.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1469-1475`
**Suggestion:** Add a `--declared-endpoint` mode to `endpoint-validator.py`/`.sh` that calls `validate_declared_endpoint`, and use it for configured providers (the built-in four keep the allowlist). The header comment at `:852-856` ("apply exactly as on the cheval path") then becomes true. The bats file covers only the 127.0.0.1 opt-in and load-time refusals; add an https non-allowlisted case.
**Benefit:** `--provider <name>` works for the hosted open-weight APIs the PR title advertises, not only loopback servers.

### 3. Budget gate — the example's contract contradicts the code

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1624` — the `budget_cents` comment still says the gate prices "ONE dissent call" and that "the companion voice … are further calls it does not count", while `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:4329-4335` now sums the primary, the companion's first hop and every advisory voice; the FR-7 paragraph a few lines below (`:1675-1683`) says the opposite of `:1624-1627`.
**File:** `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1624-1627`; `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:4320-4341`
**Suggestion:** Rewrite the `budget_cents` comment to the summed contract and state the default-config consequence: with `gpt-5.3-codex` (1.75/14 USD per Mtok in the catalog) and no Anthropic key the companion is `claude-headless` (10/50), so a 150c budget now refuses diffs above ~350 KB where it admitted up to ~430 KB before; with an Anthropic key (`opus`, 4/20) the new estimate is lower than the old fixed rate. Mention this in the CHANGELOG migration notes or raise the shipped default.
**Benefit:** Operators reading the example get the gate's real arithmetic; a mid-size diff that starts exiting 4 after the upgrade is explained.

### 4. Documentation — the CHANGELOG this PR points at is not in this PR

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/README.md:22` — the new README block links a CHANGELOG "Unreleased — earned guards and open voices" entry and `:32` tells users to "see the CHANGELOG Migration notes", but `CHANGELOG.md` is not among the 80 touched files, and this sprint changes caller-visible contracts: Bridgebuilder exit 3 now means DEGRADED and the missing-dependency preflight moved to exit 4 (`head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:161-162`, `resources/entry.sh:118-120`), `pricing_source: stale_catalog` appears in ledger rows, the dissent budget estimate changed (observation 3), and `http://` provider endpoints without an opt-in now fail config load.
**File:** `head/README.md:22-32`
**Suggestion:** Add the CHANGELOG entry and migration notes in this PR (the skill's documentation check wants one per task), covering the exit-code contract, `exit_on_degraded: 0`, the load-time endpoint rule and the budget arithmetic. If the entry already landed in an earlier sprint of cycle-129, say so in the PR description so a reviewer can verify it.
**Benefit:** The upgrade path this README promises exists where it says it does.

### 5. FAST-GATE: no record of the fast gate in the report

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md:1` — the implementation report is the PR title; it names no formatter check, type check, shellcheck, `pytest` or `bats` run. The rebuilt `dist/` (`head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/dist/.build-manifest.json`) implies `tsc` ran, but nothing shows the six new Python test files, the seven new bats files or the three TypeScript tests passing, and this workspace holds only touched files so I could not run them.
**Suggestion:** Record the self-checks (commands and results) in the report. The tests I read assert the implemented behaviour precisely (ADV-1…9, BUD-1…6, LOC-1…8, FLL-1…7, the probe, dispatcher and trusted-config suites, the local-hop E2E); the gaps are the cases named above (hosted provider labelled local; provider-block label; probe with an https configured provider; dispatcher exit 3 with empty stdout).

### 6. SIMPLICITY[shrink]: three functions well over the 50-line ceiling

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1428` — `_probe_configured` runs 118 lines (`:1428-1545`): config read, five early-return classifications, URL validation, auth selection, the curl and a four-way status switch that duplicates `_probe_openai`'s 200/401/403/other handling. `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:605` — `loadTrustedConfig` runs 110 lines (`:605-714`) mixing source selection, parsing, head-refusal, locality and exit-code validation. `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:3972` — `_adv_advisory_block` runs ~70 lines with a 25-line embedded jq program.
**Suggestion:** Split `_probe_configured` into describe/validate/auth helpers and reuse the existing OpenAI status switch; split `loadTrustedConfig` into `selectTrustedSource`, `refuseHeadOnly`, `readPosture`; move the advisory jq program to a named filter string. net: -60 lines possible.

### 7. Transport — `trust_env=False` also drops the operator's CA bundle under httpx

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:300` — for a policy hop the httpx client is built with `trust_env=False` (also `:397`, `:533`). In httpx that switch disables proxy discovery and `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` alike, while the urllib fallback still honours them through OpenSSL. An https local or opted-in hop presenting a private-CA certificate that the operator trusts via `SSL_CERT_FILE` fails TLS verification on a host with httpx installed and succeeds on one without. (Dissent DISS-C-005, confirmed against the head.)
**Suggestion:** Keep redirects and proxies off but pass an explicit `verify=ssl.create_default_context()` (which loads `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`), or disable proxies via `mounts`/`proxy=None` instead of `trust_env=False`, at the three sites; add a test with a self-signed local https stub.

### 8. Bridgebuilder vs cheval disagree on what a literal `auth` means

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:482` — any literal `auth` value without `{env:` is treated as keyless (`literalAuth`), while cheval normalises only the literal `"local"` (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:50`, `:139`) and treats any other literal as a real key. A trusted `auth: "sk-…"` provider therefore needs no env var in Bridgebuilder but is sent as a Bearer token by cheval; harmless today, but the D-8.0 doc on `ProviderDecl.keyless` (`core/types.ts:63`) states the broader rule as canonical.
**Suggestion:** Match cheval: keyless iff `keyless: true` or `auth` equals `local` (case-insensitive, trimmed).

### 9. `localhost` opt-in is resolved by the system resolver

import re,os
txt=open('pr/head.diff',encoding='utf-8',errors='replace').read()
parts=re.split(r'(?m)^(?=diff --git )',txt)

    if not p.startswith('diff --git'): continue
    m=re.match(r'diff --git a/(\S+) b/(\S+)',p)
    name=m.group(2).replace('/','__')
    open('/tmp/hunks/'+name+'.diff','w').write(p); n+=1
print(n)
EOF

+#
+# `allow_insecure_endpoint` is a host STRING naming one loopback or RFC1918 host
+# as an IP literal or `localhost` (never resolved, so no DNS rebinding). With it,
+# a URL whose host equals the opt-in host is admitted over http or https on any

# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and

Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:

 }
+# =============================================================================
+# cycle-129 FR-7 / FR-8 (SDD D-7.4, D-7.6, D-8.1): advisory voices, the catalog-priced budget gate, locality

+
+_adv_conf_advisory_voices() {  # <config key> → flatline_protocol.<key>.advisory_voices' hop names, space-separated (first
+  # occurrence kept); a non-list is said and ignored, an element that is not a hop name is said (by index and tag, never its
+  # value) and dropped — _adv_conf_chain_hops' rule. (Only the gate's own config key is spliced into the yq expressions.)
+  local config_key="$1" label="flatline_protocol.$1.advisory_voices" tg n rows="" out="" i v _nr=0

+# --- locality (D-8.1): one classification per hop, from lib/hop-locality.py over the merged catalog + project config ----
+_ADV_LOC_TSV=""       # "<hop>\t<provider>\t<local|hosted>\t<reason>" lines, this process
+_ADV_LOC_REFUSED=""   # "<role>\t<hop>\t<provider>" lines — every hosted hop refused at plan time (the envelope names them)
+_ADV_LOC_KEPT=""      # _adv_locality_filter's answer (a global: the caller runs it at top level, never in $(...))
+_adv_locality_row() { awk -F'\t' -v h="$1" '$1 == h { print; exit }' <<<"$_ADV_LOC_TSV"; }
+_adv_locality_load() {  # <hop>... — classify the hops this process has not classified yet (one python call); fail closed

+_adv_hop_is_local() { _adv_locality_load "$1"; [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$1" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; }
+_adv_locality_filter() {  # <role> <hop>... → _ADV_LOC_KEPT: the local hops in order; each hosted one is refused by name, once per role
+  local role="$1" h p; shift
+  _ADV_LOC_KEPT=""
+  _adv_locality_load "$@"
+  for h in "$@"; do
+    [[ -n "$h" ]] || continue
+    if [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$h" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; then _ADV_LOC_KEPT+="${_ADV_LOC_KEPT:+ }$h"; continue; fi

+      _ADV_LOC_REFUSED+="${role}"$'\t'"${h}"$'\t'"${p}"$'\n'

+}
+_adv_locality_refused_json() {  # → [{role, alias, provider}] for the envelope

+}
+# The one sentence the config comment and the audit output carry (D-8.1).
+_ADV_LOC_DEGRADED_SENTENCE="locality: local_voices — with one local family the companion is not an independent second voice (duplicate_voice, or not planned), so every security audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW; adversarial-review-gate.sh and verdict-derive.sh treat this envelope exactly as they treat any other."
+
+# --- the budget gate (D-7.4, D-7.6): every planned voice at its catalog price ------------------------------------------
+_ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL=0
+_ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="[]"
+_adv_budget_estimate() {  # <estimated input tokens> <role>=<hop>... → _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL (cents) and _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES (JSON);
+  # each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 output tokens × output rate (micro-USD per Mtok → cents: ÷ 10^10, each term
+  # truncated, as the fixed-rate formula was). An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok and is said;
+  # a zero-priced one estimates 0 and is said too.
+  local tokens="$1"; shift
+  local -a roles=() hops=() args=()
+  local rv rows="" line c_in c_out total=0 voices="[]"
+  for rv in "$@"; do roles+=("${rv%%=*}"); hops+=("${rv#*=}"); args+=(--alias "${rv#*=}"); done
+  if (( ${#hops[@]} > 0 )); then
+    rows=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing \
+      --catalog "${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" "${args[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  fi
+  local k _bv_role _bv_hop _bv_src _bv_in _bv_out _bv_cents
+  for (( k = 0; k < ${#hops[@]}; k++ )); do
+    _bv_role="${roles[$k]}"; _bv_hop="${hops[$k]}"   # (a role word and a validated hop name — the jq operands below are small)
+    line=$(awk -v a="alias=$_bv_hop" '$1 == a { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    _bv_in=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_out=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_src=$(sed -n 's/.* pricing_source=\([a-z_]*\)$/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    if [[ ! "$_bv_in" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || ! "$_bv_out" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || "$_bv_src" == "unknown" || -z "$_bv_src" ]]; then
+      _bv_in=10000000; _bv_out=30000000; _bv_src="fallback"
+      log "budget: no catalog price for $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice"
+    elif (( _bv_in == 0 && _bv_out == 0 )); then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c"
+    elif [[ "$_bv_src" == "stale_catalog" ]]; then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given"
+    fi
+    c_in=$(( tokens * _bv_in / 10000000000 )); c_out=$(( 2000 * _bv_out / 10000000000 )); _bv_cents=$(( c_in + c_out ))
+    total=$(( total + _bv_cents ))
+    voices=$(jq -c --arg r "$_bv_role" --arg h "$_bv_hop" --arg s "$_bv_src" --argjson c "$_bv_cents" --argjson i "$_bv_in" --argjson o "$_bv_out" \
+      '. + [{role: $r, alias: $h, estimated_cents: $c, input_per_mtok: $i, output_per_mtok: $o, pricing_source: $s}]' <<<"$voices")
+  done
+  _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL="$total"; _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="$voices"
+  log "budget: estimate ${total}c over ${#hops[@]} planned voice(s) ($(jq -r 'map("\(.role) \(.alias) \(.estimated_cents)c") | join(", ")' <<<"$voices"))"
+}
+
+# --- advisory voices (D-7.4): after the counted voices, concurrently, one wall clock, findings only under advisory_voices[] ---
+_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""   # "pid=token" pairs of the live advisory walkers (the reapers kill only the process forked)
+_adv_reap_advisory() {
+  local e p
+  for e in ${_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS:-}; do
+    p="${e%%=*}"
+    [[ "$p" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
+    _adv_is_same "$p" "$e" && { _adv_kill_tree "$p" KILL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
+  done
+  _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_advisory_walk() {  # <voice dir> <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias> — one advisory voice: the hop, then
+  # process_findings (the same schema, qualification and KF-004 repair rules as a counted voice); its rejected payloads never
+  # land beside the envelope (verdict-derive counts those), and the result is published whole
+  local d="$1" type="$2" sprint_id="$3" timeout="$4" diff_files="$5" alias="$6" raw="" rc=0 res="" st=""
+  export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REJECT_SIDECAR_DISABLE=1
+  export _ADV_SIDECAR_TAG="advisory"
+  raw=$(_adv_invoke_hop "$alias" "$d/system-prompt.txt" "$d/user-prompt.txt" "$alias" "$timeout" "$d/vq-advisory.json" "$type" "$SCRIPT_DIR/../schemas/wire/dissent-${type}.wire.json") || rc=$?
+  printf '%s' "$rc" > "$d/rc"
+  res=$(process_findings "$raw" "$type" "$alias" "$sprint_id" "$rc" "$diff_files") || res=""
+  if [[ -n "$res" ]]; then st=$(_extract_result_status "$res") || st=""; fi
+  [[ -n "$st" ]] || st="malformed_response"
+  printf '%s' "$res" > "$d/result.json.tmp" && mv -f "$d/result.json.tmp" "$d/result.json"
+  printf '%s' "$st" > "$d/status"
+}
+_adv_run_advisory_voices() {  # <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias>... — every voice started at once under
+  # $CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT seconds of wall clock for all of them; a voice still running then is killed and marked timed_out.
+  # Each voice's files are under $_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory/<n>/
+  local type="$1" sprint_id="$2" timeout="$3" diff_files="$4"; shift 4
+  local root="$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory" n=0 a d pid tok e deadline alive
+  mkdir -p "$root" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+  for a in "$@"; do
+    n=$((n + 1)); d="$root/$n"
+    mkdir -p "$d" 2>/dev/null || continue
+    printf '%s' "$a" > "$d/alias"
+    if cp -f "$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/system-prompt.txt" "$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/user-prompt.txt" "$d/" 2>/dev/null; then
+      ( _adv_advisory_walk "$d" "$type" "$sprint_id" "$timeout" "$diff_files" "$a" ) >"$d/log" 2>&1 &
+      pid=$!
+      tok=$(_adv_fork_token "$pid") || tok=""
+      _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS+="${pid}=$(_adv_tok_word "$tok") "
+      printf '%s' "$pid" > "$d/pid"
+    else
+      printf 'prompt_copy_failed' > "$d/status"
+    fi
+  done
+  deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT ))
+  while :; do
+    alive=0

+    know which vendor host that CLI reaches."""

--- DISS-C-001 MEDIUM claude-headless config | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:validate_providers
  T: 
  D: The D-7.2 rule is split into a load-time half and a request-time half, and only the OpenAI adapter implements the request-time half. An operator can declare `allow_insecure_endpoint: 10.0.0.5` on an `anthropic`-type (or any other HTTP) provider with an `http://10.0.0.5:8080` endpoint; the loader admits it, but that adapter calls `http_post`/`http_post_stream` without a `policy`, so the plaintext request honours `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` env vars (httpx default `trust_env=True`; urllib default ProxyHandler) and the urllib fallback follows 3xx redirects to any host the local server names. The prompt, and any configured credential, can therefore leave the opted-in host even though the config appears to be under the insecure-endpoint policy.
  FM: A compromised or misconfigured LAN server (or a proxy env var set in the operator's shell/CI) redirects or proxies the full prompt and Authorization header for a non-OpenAI opted-in provider to an arbitrary third party; MODELINV still records the declared destination.
--- DISS-C-002 MEDIUM claude-headless secrets | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:OpenAIAdapter.complete
  T: 
  D: A provider may carry both a real credential (`auth: {env:OPENAI_API_KEY}`, keyless false) and an `allow_insecure_endpoint` opt-in. The loader (endpoint_policy.validate_providers) admits http on any loopback or RFC1918 host, including whole 10/8 and 172.16/12 corporate ranges, with no requirement or warning that an http provider be keyless. The adapter then sends `Authorization: Bearer <real key>` in cleartext across the LAN. The opt-in was designed for keyless local servers; nothing enforces that pairing.
  FM: A copy-pasted hosted provider block repointed at an `http://10.x.x.x` proxy or test server leaks a production API key to any host on the network path; one sniffed request yields a reusable credential.
--- DISS-C-003 MEDIUM claude-headless authz | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:load_config
  T: 
  D: Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` the design (audit a257-1 MEDIUM-A1 b) says a `dispatch_group: local` model whose `fallback_chain` reaches a hosted hop must be refused at load, because cheval walks the chain inside one call. The function implementing that check exists but is not invoked from the loader path shown. cheval.py's new code uses `locality_mode_of` for telemetry only; there is no dispatch-time enforcement of local_voices in the diff either.
  FM: With locality set to local_voices, a context-window refusal or transport error on the local hop walks the fallback chain to a hosted provider and the prompt (intended to stay on-prem) is sent to a third-party API; the MODELINV row records locality_mode local_voices with a hosted destination.
--- DISS-C-004 MEDIUM claude-headless config | .claude/adapters/cheval.py:_build_provider_config
  T: 
  D: Three readers of `dispatch_group` disagree. The loader/planner rule (`hop_is_local`, `_local_labels`) accepts the label on the provider block; the adapter config builder and the MODELINV telemetry read only `models.<id>.dispatch_group`. A provider block labelled local with an https endpoint on a local host and no opt-in passes load, is planned as local, but at request time no TransportPolicy is applied (proxy env honoured, urllib follows redirects) and the audit row records hop_locality `hosted`.
  FM: A hop the planner and the operator believe is local egresses through an environment proxy or a redirect, and the MODELINV audit chain says it was hosted, so the discrepancy is invisible to later review.
--- DISS-C-005 LOW claude-headless other | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:destination_for
  T: 
  D: destination_for records `{host: cli-subprocess, scheme: cli}` whenever the provider is absent from the hounfour view or has an empty endpoint, not only for genuine CLI hops. A hop whose provider name is not in `hounfour.providers` (hand-built config, alias mismatch, or a `final_model_id` whose provider segment differs from the catalog key) is written into the tamper-evident MODELINV chain as a local CLI subprocess even if it went over HTTP to a remote host.
  FM: Audit consumers filtering for hosted egress miss HTTP hops mislabelled as CLI; the record is confidently wrong rather than `unknown`.
--- DISS-C-006 LOW claude-headless input-validation | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:_names_response_format
  T: 
  D: Any HTTP 400 whose body contains the substring `response_format` or `json_schema` (case-insensitive, any field) causes the adapter to drop the strict output schema and re-send the full prompt. The server controls this trigger. A local or opted-in server can therefore force schema enforcement off at will, and the retry doubles prompt transmission and spend. Telemetry does record schema_rejected_by_server, so this is a downgrade the operator can see but cannot prevent.
  FM: A misbehaving server returns a generic 400 mentioning json_schema; cheval silently falls back to the tolerant parser and repair loop, consuming budget on a second full request.
--- DISS-C-007 LOW claude-headless info-disclosure | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:describe_provider
  T: 
  D: describe_provider prints the provider endpoint verbatim to stdout for the health-probe shell script. For CLI providers (`*-headless` or all `kind: cli`) the endpoint is never validated, and for HTTP providers the validator's handling of query strings and fragments is not asserted here, so a URL carrying a token in its query (`?api_key=...`) would be emitted to logs by a command documented as never printing a secret.
  FM: Probe output captured in CI logs exposes a credential embedded in an endpoint URL.

--- DISS-C-002 MEDIUM claude-headless secrets | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:OpenAIAdapter.complete
  T: 
  D: A provider may carry both a real credential (`auth: {env:OPENAI_API_KEY}`, keyless false) and an `allow_insecure_endpoint` opt-in. The loader (endpoint_policy.validate_providers) admits http on any loopback or RFC1918 host, including whole 10/8 and 172.16/12 corporate ranges, with no requirement or warning that an http provider be keyless. The adapter then sends `Authorization: Bearer <real key>` in cleartext across the LAN. The opt-in was designed for keyless local servers; nothing enforces that pairing.
  FM: A copy-pasted hosted provider block repointed at an `http://10.x.x.x` proxy or test server leaks a production API key to any host on the network path; one sniffed request yields a reusable credential.
--- DISS-C-003 MEDIUM claude-headless authz | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:load_config
  T: 
  D: Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` the design (audit a257-1 MEDIUM-A1 b) says a `dispatch_group: local` model whose `fallback_chain` reaches a hosted hop must be refused at load, because cheval walks the chain inside one call. The function implementing that check exists but is not invoked from the loader path shown. cheval.py's new code uses `locality_mode_of` for telemetry only; there is no dispatch-time enforcement of local_voices in the diff either.
  FM: With locality set to local_voices, a context-window refusal or transport error on the local hop walks the fallback chain to a hosted provider and the prompt (intended to stay on-prem) is sent to a third-party API; the MODELINV row records locality_mode local_voices with a hosted destination.
--- DISS-C-004 MEDIUM claude-headless config | .claude/adapters/cheval.py:_build_provider_config
  T: 
  D: Three readers of `dispatch_group` disagree. The loader/planner rule (`hop_is_local`, `_local_labels`) accepts the label on the provider block; the adapter config builder and the MODELINV telemetry read only `models.<id>.dispatch_group`. A provider block labelled local with an https endpoint on a local host and no opt-in passes load, is planned as local, but at request time no TransportPolicy is applied (proxy env honoured, urllib follows redirects) and the audit row records hop_locality `hosted`.
  FM: A hop the planner and the operator believe is local egresses through an environment proxy or a redirect, and the MODELINV audit chain says it was hosted, so the discrepancy is invisible to later review.
--- DISS-C-005 LOW claude-headless other | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:destination_for
  T: 
  D: destination_for records `{host: cli-subprocess, scheme: cli}` whenever the provider is absent from the hounfour view or has an empty endpoint, not only for genuine CLI hops. A hop whose provider name is not in `hounfour.providers` (hand-built config, alias mismatch, or a `final_model_id` whose provider segment differs from the catalog key) is written into the tamper-evident MODELINV chain as a local CLI subprocess even if it went over HTTP to a remote host.
  FM: Audit consumers filtering for hosted egress miss HTTP hops mislabelled as CLI; the record is confidently wrong rather than `unknown`.
--- DISS-C-006 LOW claude-headless input-validation | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:_names_response_format
  T: 
  D: Any HTTP 400 whose body contains the substring `response_format` or `json_schema` (case-insensitive, any field) causes the adapter to drop the strict output schema and re-send the full prompt. The server controls this trigger. A local or opted-in server can therefore force schema enforcement off at will, and the retry doubles prompt transmission and spend. Telemetry does record schema_rejected_by_server, so this is a downgrade the operator can see but cannot prevent.
  FM: A misbehaving server returns a generic 400 mentioning json_schema; cheval silently falls back to the tolerant parser and repair loop, consuming budget on a second full request.
--- DISS-C-007 LOW claude-headless info-disclosure | .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:describe_provider
  T: 
  D: describe_provider prints the provider endpoint verbatim to stdout for the health-probe shell script. For CLI providers (`*-headless` or all `kind: cli`) the endpoint is never validated, and for HTTP providers the validator's handling of query strings and fragments is not asserted here, so a URL carrying a token in its query (`?api_key=...`) would be emitted to logs by a command documented as never printing a secret.
  FM: Probe output captured in CI logs exposes a credential embedded in an endpoint URL.

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

Scope: `pr/head.diff` — PR sprint-257 (cycle-129), 80 files (23 generated `dist/` artefacts), 6,606 insertions / 221 deletions. Citations are `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers from `pr/head/`. Prerequisite note: the review (`engineer-feedback.md`) ended CHANGES_REQUIRED, so the skill's Phase 0 gate ("All good") is not met; the task instruction orders this audit to run regardless, and it has, with the review's two blocking findings re-verified independently below. `grimoires/loa/known-failures.md` is absent (WARN at session start); `br` is not installed; no documentation-coherence subagent reports exist, so the documentation checks were done by hand (SKILL.md, README, `.loa.config.yaml.example`, the two reference docs, the MODELINV schema).

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The sprint adds four security-relevant mechanisms: a per-provider insecure-endpoint opt-in with a request-time TransportPolicy, the `hounfour.locality: local_voices` confidentiality posture, Bridgebuilder's trusted-configuration source for provider declarations, and keyless/open-weight providers with advisory dissent voices. The endpoint rule itself is sound where it is applied: I ran the head validator against the shipped default endpoints (all admit, including the templated Bedrock host) and an opt-in edge table (host mismatch, userinfo, traversal, metadata, IPv6 ULA, `host:port` opt-ins all refused), the shell operands that reach `jq`/`yq`/`python3` are validated or passed as files, and the PR's six Python suites pass in a head-over-framework tree (123 tests).

Two findings block the merge, both re-verified against the head and both also raised by the review. First, `local_voices` is decided by a label: a provider whose endpoint is `https://api.together.xyz/v1` and whose model carries `dispatch_group: local` is classified `local` by `hop-locality.py`, accepted by `validate_providers`, dispatched by cheval, and recorded as `hop_locality: local` in MODELINV; cheval reads the locality switch for telemetry only and never enforces it, and the label is read from different places by the planners and the transport. Second, Bridgebuilder's trusted configuration governs its planner only; every voice still dispatches through cheval, which loads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`, so the new SKILL.md sentence promising trusted precedence "even when the checkout is a PR head" is not delivered.

The cross-model dissent (two voices, `gpt-5.5-pro` + `claude-headless`, 7 findings, none rejected) added one medium of its own: the loader admits `allow_insecure_endpoint` on any HTTP provider type while only the OpenAI adapter applies the TransportPolicy. No critical finding; nothing excluded from the tally.

**Security Issues Found:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 2 |
| Medium | 6 |
| Low | 11 |

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] The `local_voices` posture is a declaration, not a verified property

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116` (classifier); the same label-only rule at `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:476` (`hop_locality_of`), `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:221` (`_transport_policy`), `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726` (`isLocalVoice`); the label read from the model entry only at `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:541`; no load-time refusal at `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:143` (`validate_providers`).
**Issue:** The classifier's rule is
```python
group = entry.get("dispatch_group") or block.get("dispatch_group") or ""
if group != "local":
    return provider, "hosted", f"dispatch_group={group or 'unset'}"
```
(`hop-locality.py:116-118`). Nothing examines the endpoint. Reproduced against the head with the shipped catalog plus this overlay:
```yaml
hounfour:
  locality: local_voices
  providers:
    hosted-oss:
      type: openai_compat
      endpoint: "https://api.together.xyz/v1"
      auth: "{env:LOA_TOGETHER_KEY}"
      models:
        llama-70b: {dispatch_group: local, context_window: 131072}
```
```
$ python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog model-config.yaml --config overlay.yaml -- hosted-oss:llama-70b
hosted-oss:llama-70b	hosted-oss	local	dispatch_group=local
$ validate_providers(overlay)   # endpoint_policy.py:143
(no error)
```
